title: Underlying vector of the normalized projection
statement: Let $V$ be a real inner product space, let $u \in V$ be a unit vector, and let $v \in V$. Write $w = v - \langle u, v\rangle\, u$ for the component of $v$ orthogonal to $u$. The normalized vector $\norm{w}^{-1} w$, regarded as an element of the orthogonal complement $(\mathrm{span}_{\bbr}\{u\})^{\perp}$ of the line spanned by $u$, has underlying vector in $V$ equal to $\norm{w}^{-1} w$.
hypotheses_covered: V is a real inner product space
v is an arbitrary vector in V
